c.tagline: Bulgaria's sea capital — Black Sea beaches, Roman baths, and the world's oldest gold.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are yellow and metered by law; use marked companies or apps like TaxiMe and check the meter is running to avoid inflated tourist rates. Uber does not operate in Bulgaria.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide single emergency number and works for all services (police, fire, ambulance) throughout Bulgaria.

avoid.reason: Watch your drinks and bar bills in the Golden Sands nightlife strip and guard valuables on crowded summer beaches.

hood_desc: The walkable core around the Cathedral of the Assumption, the pedestrian Knyaz Boris I boulevard, the Roman Baths, and the Archaeological Museum that holds the Varna gold treasure; best for first-timers.
The seafront district (Primorski) wrapping the Sea Garden park, city beach, dolphinarium, and marina; the summer heart for beach days and evening strolls.
A leafy residential quarter above the Sea Garden with hotels, restaurants, and quick access to the beach; relaxed and popular with visitors.
A district across the bay by the port with its own long sandy beach and a village feel; quieter and away from the tourist core.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though many locals prefer bottled for taste.

transit.hours: City buses and trolleybuses run from roughly 5:00 AM to around 11:00 PM; taxis and ride apps fill the late-night gap.
transit.note: Varna has no metro or tram; the city is served by an extensive network of buses and electric trolleybuses. Trolleybus lines 12, 82, 83 and 88 serve the Sea Garden, and the compact centre is easily walked.
transit.pay: Pay the flat fare in cash to the conductor or driver (around 2 lev per ride), or tap a contactless bank card on newer vehicles; keep small change handy.

tip.r: Rounding up or leaving ~10% for good service in restaurants is common; not expected for taxis.

landmarks: Dormition of the Mother of God Cathedral
Varna's gold-domed 1886 cathedral, Bulgaria's second largest, dominates the city centre with its striped facade, murals and glittering onion domes.
Sea Garden (Morska Gradina)
A vast landscaped park stretching along the Black Sea cliffs, threading monuments, an aquarium and shady promenades between the city and its beaches.
Varna Archaeological Museum
Home of the Varna Gold, the world's oldest worked gold treasure at over 6,000 years, alongside superb Thracian, Greek and Roman collections.
Roman Thermae
The imposing 2nd-century ruins of the largest Roman bath complex in the Balkans, its brick arches rising unexpectedly amid the old Greek quarter.
Euxinograd Palace and Gardens
A late-19th-century royal summer residence in French château style, set in exquisite seaside gardens and vineyards north of the city.
Naval Museum and the Druzki Torpedo Boat
Bulgaria's maritime story told beside the Sea Garden, starring the preserved torpedo boat Druzki, which famously struck an Ottoman cruiser in 1912.
Retro Museum
A nostalgic romp through Bulgaria's socialist era, packed with gleaming vintage cars, communist memorabilia and waxworks of Eastern Bloc leaders.
Asparuhov Bridge and Asparuhovo Beach
The soaring 1976 bridge spanning Varna's shipping canal, a city emblem best admired from the long sandy beach and park beneath it.
Clock Tower of Varna
A 24-meter tower near the cathedral, originally built as a fire watchpost and rebuilt in 1888, still marking the center of the old town.
Dolphinarium
A futuristic glass-fronted arena set in the Sea Garden where Black Sea bottlenose dolphins perform, a striking modern landmark on the city's wooded seafront.

train.note: No international train currently serves Varna directly; for Bucharest or Istanbul you change at Ruse or Gorna Oryahovitsa, or route yourself the long way through Sofia. Varna Central, an art nouveau building of 1925 next to the port at the southern edge of the centre, has several daily trains to Sofia taking 7.5-8.5 hours through the Iskar Gorge, including an overnight service with sleeping and couchette cars that is much the most civilised way to do it. Direct trains also run to Plovdiv, Ruse and Shumen. Fares are cheap and tickets can be bought on the day at the station or on bdz.bg, but note that the coach beats the train to Sofia by two hours or more.

bus.note: The Central Bus Station is about 2 km northwest of the seafront on Vladislav Varnenchik Boulevard, and works as a hall of individual operator ticket offices rather than one central desk, so shop around the windows. Coaches to Istanbul take roughly 9-10 hours, often overnight via the Malko Tarnovo or Kapitan Andreevo crossings, where everyone leaves the bus for passport control; arrange a Turkish e-visa beforehand. Domestic services to Sofia (6-7 hours), Burgas, Plovdiv and Veliko Tarnovo run through the day, with Union Ivkoni (https://www.union-ivkoni.com/) and Etap Grup among the main carriers. Booking online a day ahead is worth it in July and August when the coast fills up.

intl.to: Poti & Batumi (Georgia) - sails from Port Varna-East, walking distance from the city centre

ferry.note: Varna is Bulgaria's only regular passenger port, but the service is a Navibulgar ro-ro freight ship that carries a limited number of passengers and vehicles rather than a conventional ferry, so expect a cargo timetable and basic cabins. Because of the war in Ukraine the Georgian run to Poti and Batumi is the only line still operating, leaving at roughly ten-day intervals and taking about two days at sea. Book directly with the company well in advance, particularly if you are bringing a vehicle, and allow for departures slipping by a day or more. The terminal in Port Varna-East is a short walk from the Sea Garden and the railway station; cruise ships also call here but are not usable as scheduled transport.

half.name: Aladzha Monastery
half.blurb: A medieval cave monastery hewn into a sheer karst cliff near Golden Sands, its chambers and chapel niches linked by vertiginous stairways.

half.name: Pobiti Kamani (The Stone Forest)
half.blurb: An eerie desert-like plain of natural limestone columns formed 50 million years ago, standing like ruined temple pillars just west of the city.
